script: [serious] His last words over the radio were: it's not an aircraft. Then a strange metallic noise. And then nothing. October 21st, 1978. Twenty-year-old pilot Frederick Valentich took off from Melbourne in a small Cessna, heading across the Bass Strait to King Island. It was getting dark. At seven-oh-six, he called air traffic control. Something was near him. A large aircraft, he said, with four bright lights. Controllers told him there was no known traffic at his height. He said it was orbiting him. That it had a green light, and it looked metallic. Then he reported his engine was rough idling. Asked to identify the object, he said: it's hovering, and it's not an aircraft. The microphone stayed open. Controllers heard what they described as a metallic noise. Then silence. Ships and planes searched over a thousand square miles. No wreck. No pilot. Years later, part of an engine cowl washed up on an island that may have come from his plane. Skeptics say he became disoriented in the dark and spiraled into the sea. Others say he saw something real. What did he see? You decide. This is Dossier Decoded. Case file number twenty-eight. A new file every day.
